chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Waiting by the garbage cans to see the Senator
summary: Because they were Black, Danny, Lu and Paul had to enter the Senator's hotel through the basement and waited hours, and Lu refused to return.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So Senator Lebeau was living at the New Orleans Hotel. Papa Stoppa said, "You go to the New Orleans Hotel, and he's there." I go to the New Orleans Hotel, and you're not allowed to go through the front elevator. So me and Paul...

Me, you and Paul. Because they wanted him to bring me, because he was supposed to bring me a watch. So we go to the hotel, and we couldn't go through the front door. So we had to go around. So we're finally in the basement. I'm all sharp, you know, and I was young...

Around the garbage cans. We're standing up there waiting for the Senator to send for us. So we were there, I don't know, about two hours, maybe three hours waiting for him to call. So I told them, I said, "Look, you'all can stay if you'all want, but I'm going." They said, "Well, the Senator said..." So we told them that we were going. So they said "The Senator said come back tomorrow." See?
So the next day I told Paul and Danny, I said, "Now, if you'all want to go amongst them garbage cans down there
waiting for the Senator, you'all can do. But I ain't goin'. I'm gonna stay home." Now you can take over.
